2.text: This knife is similar to the crooked knife of the Alaskan Eskimo.¹ It

3.text: is used with the same characteristic motion of the hand toward the body which

4.text: the Chukchee employs when using the ordinary knife. The Russian and the

5.text: Russianized Yukaghir, on the contrary, move the knife away from the body.

6.text: A knife quite similar in shape to the Chukchee crooked knife (Fig. 132, d)

7.text: is used by the Russians on the Kolyma and Anadyr for the special purpose

8.text: of finishing the hollowed tree-trunks scooped out for canoes. This knife is

9.text: often grasped with both hands, and it is moved away from the body, as are

10.text: the other knives used by these tribes. An adze of peculiar shape is used by

11.text: the Russians for the rougher part of this work. One variety of this crooked

12.text: knife (Fig. 132, e) is commonly used by all tribes of northeastern Asia for

14.text: Neither the Chukchee nor the other tribes have special tools used only

15.text: for carving or engraving ivory or bone. This work is done with various

16.text: knives, crooked or straight, but those with short slender blades are preferred.
